To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the novel thieno [3,2-d ] pyrimidine and quinozoline derivatives containing N -acylhydrazones and semicarbaones were designed, synthesized and evaluated for antitumor activity and compound 14 showed potent antitumor activity against HT-29, MDA-MB -231, U87 MG, PC-3, and HCT- 116 cell lines.

the novel thieno [3,2-d ] pyrimidine and quinzoline derivatives containing N-acetylhydrazone or N-succinimidyl semicarbazones were designed and synthesized, and evaluated their antitumor activities in vitro and in vivo, and the structure-activity relationships (SARs) of the target molecules were also investigated.
the most potent antineoplastic compound 14 was identified from a series of N-acylthieno[3.2-d]pyridazine and N-acylquinazoline derivatives.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel thienopyrimidine and quinozoline derivatives with potent antitumor activity.
the design and synthesis of novel thienopyrimidine and quinaoline derivatives containing N-acylhydrazones or semicarbaones.
the discovery of new thieno[2,3-d]pyrimidines and quinazolines derivatives as potential antitumor drugs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the thieno [3,2-d]-pyrimidine derivatives 14 and 15 are potent PI3K inhibitors, which can induce cell cycle arrest and cell apoptosis in HCC cells.
thieno [3,2-d ]pyrimidine and N-acetylhydrazine or semicarboxylate are optimal fragments for the development of new anticancer agents.
compound 14 is the first potent PI3Kα inhibitor with antitumor activities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we designed, synthesized and evaluated a series of thieno[2,3-d]pyrimidines and quinazolines containing N-acylhazone or semicarboxylic acid, and the results of biological evaluation showed that compound 14 exhibited the most potent antiproliferative activity with IC50 values ranging from 0.22 to 1.78 μM against five human cancer cell lines.
the novel thieno-[3,2-d]-pyrimidine and 2,4-diaminopteridin-6-one derivatives are potential antitumor agents with the ability to induce G2/M cell cycle arrest and cell apoptosis in HCC cells.
the novel thieno [3,2-d]-pyrimidine and 6-aminoquinazoline derivatives containing the N-acyl-hydrazone or semecarbazone moiety were designed, synthesized and evaluated for their antitumor activities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
thieno-pyrimidine and quinoxaline derivatives with N-acyl-hydrazine or semicarbarazone moiety could be promising candidates for the design and synthesis of antitumor agents.
thieno [3,2-d]-pyrimidine and N-acyl semicarbazones are potential scaffolds for antitumor drug design.
the thieno [3,2-d ]pyrimidine and N-acyl hydrazone/semicarbazone moiety are important pharmacophores for the design of novel antitumor agents with potential clinical applications.
